To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the school counselor is a critical component of a systemic approach to promoting cultural responsiveness in schools.

the school counselor's role in promoting systemic cultural responsiveness in schools requires a shift in focus from individual student counseling to a focus on the school system and its impact on student success.
school counselors can be effective in creating systemic change and culturally responsive schools.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways that school counselors can be effective in promoting cultural responsiveness in schools and the strategies they can use to do so.
the development of a new paradigm for school counseling that promotes systemic change, and that fosters culturally responsive school environments that are inclusive, equitable, and empowering.
the ways in which the school counselor, in partnership with the school, parents, and community, can promote cultural responsiveness.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the school counselor is the catalyst for change and the advocate for all students.
the role of the multicultural school counselor is one that requires an understanding of the school system, its culture, and the culture of the students served.
the role of the counselor is not to be a "counselor" in the traditional sense of the word, but rather to be an advocate, a consultant, a collaborator, a change agent, and a leader.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a model that can serve as a guide to help schools become more culturally responsive.
the school counselor can be an agent of change in the school system and in the classroom to promote cultural responsiveness and culturally responsive teaching.

we are committed to the development of a school counseling program and school counseling curriculum which promotes the cultural competence of the school counselor, school staff, and students and which promotes the cultural responsiveness of the school community.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the school counselor is a critical change agent for promoting cultural responsiveness in schools.
school counselors can be a catalyst for systemic change in schools by promoting cultural responsiveness.
the school counselor must be a leader of change and a catalyst for systemic change to promote cultural responsiveness and student achievement in our schools.
